IGNIS is an interactive spacecraft fire-safety intelligence platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archives. To address fragmented test logs, mixed unit systems, and AI hallucination risks, we standardized 892 experiments (840 measured tests and 52 modeled partial-gravity rows excluded by default) across 24 NASA PSI investigations and 30 dataset families into a canonical 44-column SI schema paired with 31 mission dossiers.

Built with FastAPI and React 19, IGNIS provides six interactive modules: an Overview comparing normal-gravity and microgravity flame regimes; an Explorer summarizing fixed versus varied parameters and sensor measurements; a Physics Lab comparing PSI study objectives, hardware rigs (CIR, MDCA, MSG), and historical spacecraft fires; a 2D Risk Simulator modeling flammability boundaries, NASA-STD-6001 limits, detection and suppression trade-offs (SAME, DAFT-2, SLICE, SAFFIRE), and exportable safety dossiers; an Analytics audit dashboard; and Ask IGNIS, a citation-locked Hybrid SQL and RAG assistant.

This is critical because microgravity eliminates buoyancy, lowering oxygen flammability thresholds and altering smoke behavior as Artemis lunar habitats adopt higher oxygen atmospheres.

What It Does & How It Works

IGNIS (Flame in Freefall) turns fragmented NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity fire-safety data into a zero-hallucination simulator, investigation explorer, and AI research assistant.

Instead of forcing engineers or students to dig through incompatible spreadsheets and PDFs, we standardized 892 combustion experiments (840 measured orbital/ground tests + 52 modeled partial-gravity rows separated by default) across 24 NASA PSI investigations, 30 dataset families, and 31 mission dossiers into a single 44-column SI schema.

The platform delivers six focused tools:

  • Overview: Side-by-side 1g vs. 0g flame physics comparator and live telemetry samples.
  • Explorer: Searchable 892-row catalog with an automatic Fixed vs. Varied Variables & Sensor Summary and full provenance drawer.
  • Physics Lab: Compares historical spacecraft fires (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir), family criticality, live PSI CSV tables, and a side-by-side comparator across all 24 PSI investigations.
  • Risk Simulator: Interactive 2D flammability contour maps (12%–100% O₂, 20–120 kPa), NASA-STD-6001 comparison, Detection & Suppression Advisor (SAME, DAFT-2, SLICE, SAFFIRE), and one-click PDF/Markdown Safety Dossier export.
  • Analytics: Corpus quality audit, Earth/Moon/Spacesuit atmosphere bars, and NASA hardware mappings.
  • Ask IGNIS: Hybrid SQL + dense/BM25 RAG assistant where every number and [ID] citation is programmatically verified—no fabricated data.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Faster, Safer Habitat Design: As NASA shifts from ISS air (21% O₂) to oxygen-enriched Artemis lunar habitats (≥30% O₂, ≤10.2 psi) and spacesuits (100% O₂, 4.3 psi), zero buoyancy lowers ignition limits and changes smoke size. IGNIS makes decades of PSI data immediately actionable for aerospace engineers, researchers, professors, and students.
  • Works 100% Offline: Runs deterministic SQL, local BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings, and ML inference locally with zero external API dependency (with optional Ollama/Anthropic support).

Tools & Tech Stack

  • Backend & Data: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, Apache Parquet (PyArrow), Pandas, Pandera, SQLite.
  • AI & Physics ML: scikit-learn (Random Forest ensembles + 5-NN), SentenceTransformers (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5), Okapi BM25 + RRF search, NumPy.
  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, HTML5 <canvas> (60 FPS 0g flame orb & clickable 2D maps), plus a companion Streamlit + Plotly dashboard.
  • Verification: Pytest, Vitest, and a 65-question golden RAG/SQL benchmark.

Creativity & Key Considerations

  • Physics-Informed ML: Rather than treating combustion as a black box, our simulator injects Oxygen Partial Pressure (PO2), N2/02, and a non-monotonic Peclet flow curve (modeling both quiescent starvation and high-flow blowoff) alongside 90% prediction intervals.
  • Hardware & Atmosphere Nuances Built In: Groups shared flight rigs (CIR, CIR-MDCA, MSG Flow Duct), contrasts smoke vs. lunar dust instruments (SAME vs. DAFT), quarantines 42 corrupt BASS-II airflow spikes, prevents incompatible burn-rate comparisons across fuels, and flags partial-gravity gaps (LUCI, FM2, E-FIELD) instead of hiding them.
